title: effect_pan clamps the pan target at the live zoom, not the target zoom — mid-ease pans converge outside the world rect
detail: The center converges with cam_zoom_to but is validated against the eased cam_zoom; camera_update never re-clamps. A drag during any zoom-out ease (including the pullback window) converges with the viewport past the world edge — void plus cut-off map.
recommended_fix: Clamp the pan target at app.cam_zoom_to (keep converting the delta at the live zoom per W5), or re-clamp the center in camera_update once converged.

title: pullback_feed caps spawn-event mapping at 8 ids — a 9+ spawn frame silently skips the pullback
detail: camera_newest_terminals stops at len(ids)=8; with nine-plus NODE_SPAWNED events in one frame found != n_spawns and the feed returns — a genuine seed in a large catch-up burst never pulls back.
recommended_fix: Grow the id buffer with n_spawns (dynamic, or a bounded cap that processes the events it can) instead of silently dropping the whole frame's pullback.

title: stale-latch guard can synthesize a Mouse_Release every frame if placement is armed while the pan latch is live
evidence:
} else if pan_latch_stale(inp.panning, rl.IsMouseButtonDown(.LEFT)) {

		} else if inp.panning && !drag_eff && placing_eff < 0 {
detail: The synthesized release clears the latch only via the pan branch, which requires placing_eff < 0; no placement-path clear is visible. With placement armed while the latch is stranded, a release is appended every frame.
recommended_fix: Clear inp.panning inside the stale-guard branch itself (or when placement arms) so the synthesized release cannot re-fire indefinitely.

title: "at any z_to the clamp is a no-op for a zoom-out" contradicted by the diff's own B1 pin
detail: The B1 pin moves cy from 585 to 390 at z_to=1.0 — a zoom-out — so the clamp demonstrably moves the center; it compares against the world rect, not prior half-extents. The comment's mechanism is wrong.
recommended_fix: Rewrite: the clamp runs at the target zoom and can move the center (pins at the fit, bounds elsewhere); inclusion follows from the world-rect viewport, not no-op preservation.

title: PR body's new-pin counts (4+4+4+2) don't match the diff's own new test files (9+7+7+2)
evidence:
- New pins: 4 camera-math tests (app/render/camera_test.odin) + 4 input
  wiring tests (app/input/camera_input_test.odin) + 4 pullback tests
  (app/pullback_test.odin — seed/attach discrimination, the toggle, the
  already-visible no-op, and the no-snap ease + convergence) + 2 settings
  tests
detail: The diff's own new files declare 9, 7, 7 and 2 @(test) procs respectively; all four are new in this diff, so the claimed per-file counts are checkable and wrong.
recommended_fix: Correct the PR body's verification counts to the actual per-file test counts.

title: pullback test drives effect_settings_adjust with no settings path injected — may write the real user settings file
detail: The fixture zeroes the App and injects no settings path, yet the adjust hook persists on every change; unlike the exec-level adjust tests, this one can write the default user settings file.
recommended_fix: Inject a temporary settings path in pullback_test_app (the exec-test pattern) so the toggle leg cannot clobber the real settings file.

title: "four constants" ungated — five NOC constants sit outside the PP_DEBUG gate
evidence:

detail: NOC_PANEL_X/Y/W/H plus NOC_ROW_H — five constants — are moved outside the gate; the comment claims four. Only the hit test needs the geometry quadruple.

title: Pan executor has no draw guard — a two-finger touch pan can pan the camera mid-draw, unlike the mouse path
detail: mouse_map emits Pan only when no draw is active (the !drag_eff gate); the executor routes every Pan intent unconditionally, so a two-finger pan during a touch draw pans mid-gesture with no visible guard.
recommended_fix: Gate the Pan executor on !inp.drag.active (or cancel the draw on second-finger touch) to match the mouse path's gesture ownership.
